Next Economy Lab develops and implements concepts for a socially just, climate-positive, and collaborative economy in partnership with policymakers, businesses, trade unions, and civil society. Sustainability, personal responsibility, and collaborative leadership are the core principles that guide our work. That is why we are looking for people who share these values and are passionate about driving sustainable transformation. The project The project examines the global implications of current industrial policy. It focuses on the question of how such policy can be shaped in the context of a globally just socio-ecological transformation (Just Transition) that takes existing power relations and postcolonial structures into account and opens up new perspectives on economic development. To this end, the project will bring together representatives from academia, labor unions, development cooperation, and civil society from the Global North and South for two roundtable discussions and a two-day international conference in Bonn. These specialized formats are complemented by a public film screening and discussion event, a five-part blog series, and a policy brief that summarizes key findings and formulates concrete recommendations for policymakers and development practitioners. Your internship Responsibilities The specific responsibilities of your internship will be agreed individually, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and availability, and may include the following areas: Support the preparation and implementation of a 2-day international conference located in Bonn in cooperation with IDOS (e.g. participant management and communication, evaluation) Support the preparation and implementation of 2 roundtable discussions and a public evening event Support public relations activities (e.g. creating social media posts, blog articles and video documentation) What we are looking for Ability to work independently and reliably Strong communication and teamwork skills Previous knowledge or strong interest in the project topic Experience in event organisation is desirable Fluent English language skills, preferably also German What we offer We are a small, motivated team that offers plenty of opportunities to take on responsibility and grow both professionally and personally. The internship is compensated with an expense allowance We value a supportive and appreciative feedback and working culture. We offer internships lasting at least three months, exclusively as mandatory internships, with flexible working hours. Application process If you are interested, please send us your CV, employment references and a one-page letter of motivation. You may also optionally include supporting documents demonstrating relevant professional experience (e.g. training certificates, descriptions of responsibilities in previous positions or similar documents). Please send your application by email with the subject line “Student Assistant FEB Industrial Policy” to: Jonas Bothe (bothe@nexteconomylab.de). Please do not include a photograph in your CV. Diversity We are committed to social justice and strive to reflect this commitment in our recruitment processes. We particularly encourage applications from FLINTA* people (women, lesbians, intersex, non-binary, trans and agender people), Black, Indigenous and People of Colour (BIPoC), and people with disabilities.
